prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional molecules bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell destroys it

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I still hold B068 as the best match to my standard of a game-changer: a new principle (removal by induced proximity instead of inhibition), stated in simple chemical terms, reproduced by many independent groups, with design rules (ligand, linker, ternary-complex cooperativity) that are quantitative and transferable. The chair's question on timing is fair, and my answer is that the absence of an approved degrader is a reason to word the citation around the mechanism of degradation and the design principle, not the clinical pipeline. The citation I now propose says that explicitly and does not promise medicines. Crews and Deshaies established the concept and first proofs, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex analysis are what made the principle general and rational. Three names give one coherent, explainable message, and B068 has the broadest opening support on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the medical consequences are still promised rather than demonstrated, and a more cautious committee could reasonably wait a few years. The three-name limit forces a contestable cut: Sakamoto shares the 2001 proof of concept, and Handa, Ito, Kim and Gray carry the cereblon and glue strand that is scientifically fundamental. If the committee weights settled maturity and attribution above newness, B057 is the safer and cleaner choice, and I would not regard that as an error. B068 also leaves its own third place open between Ciulli and Handa, and that is a real scientific judgment, not a formality.

responses.point: Chabes argues that PROTACs and cereblon-based glues share one E3-redirection mechanism, so a single citation can cover both and Handa should hold the third place.
responses.response: The shared mechanism is real, and I accept that a mechanism-level citation brings the glue strand into view. I still distinguish two things: the cereblon discovery explains why thalidomide-type drugs work, which is a mechanistic insight about existing drugs, whereas the PROTAC concept is a designable principle that anyone can apply to a new target. A prize for design needs the person who made design general, and I judge that to be Ciulli, through VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures. Taking Handa would mean dropping Crews or Deshaies, and I will not displace the originators. I answer the chair's question this way: one citation can honestly name induced degradation through E3 recruitment, but only two strands in a single sentence would be overstated. I keep the Ciulli seat, and I would support wording that does not exclude glues.

responses.point: Somfai holds that C-N coupling needed its own mechanistic and ligand solution (amine binding, difficult C-N reductive elimination), so it is a distinct discovery from the 2010 C-C prize, with Kosugi and Migita at most acknowledged in the background.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument for B057 and I take it seriously: the C-N reductive elimination problem was genuinely hard, and ligand design solved it in a way that is quantitative and general. I also agree that Kosugi and Migita should be handled in the background text and by the words general and catalytic, not by crediting them. Where we differ is on what counts as newness. I read B057 as a major sequel within a concept already honoured in 2010, whereas induced-proximity degradation is a new way of using a cellular process as a chemical tool. I accept that a committee that puts maturity and clean attribution first could reasonably go the other way, and B057 stays as my first alternative.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, prefers phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation, with a citation held to the organising principle and not to condensate functions.
responses.response: I appreciate that you hold the citation to the principle, and I agree that the founding observation of liquid P granules is solid. My difficulty is the one you list yourself: in-vitro demixing is well quantified, but functional liquid-liquid phase separation in living cells is not yet separated from artefacts of overexpression and crowding. Degrader mechanism has a direct readout in degradation kinetics, ternary-complex formation and E3 dependence that has held up across laboratories. In my view the evidence base for B068 is more mature on that specific point, though I would not call B022 wrong, only a few years early. I do not move on this.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers energy-landscape theory of protein folding (Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht) as a mature, mechanism-level physical principle complementary to the 2024 prize.
responses.response: As a theorist I share your respect for the funnel picture, and I ranked it fifth for that reason. What holds me back is the credit problem, since Bryngelson and Dill have priority claims, and it pairs theory with experiment in a way the chair questions. I also doubt that the funnel predicted more than folding kinetics already showed, so its consequences for chemistry beyond conceptual clarity are less visible than for degraders. I would keep B027 behind B068 and B057, though it remains a respectable fallback and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Sparr stresses that phase separation is measured through chemical quantities (valency, saturation concentration, material properties) and prefers Rosen over Pappu for the third place.
responses.response: I agree that many of those measurements are chemical and that Rosen's multivalent-grammar work is the better-attributed third name than a sequence-based alternative. My reservation is not whether the quantities are chemical but whether the cellular claim is settled. On credit, Pappu and Mittag are excluded by the three-name limit under any configuration, which makes the B022 citation harder to defend than the three-person count suggests.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize before any degrader is approved, or whether it prefers to wait a few years.
Whether the third place should be Ciulli or Handa, and how much weight Sakamoto's 2001 proof of concept deserves.
Whether the committee can phrase one citation that honours degradation by induced proximity without overstating the glue strand.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent: none of the B068 candidates is among my listed connections (Warshel, the Uppsala RNA and ribosome community, Brzezinski). The round-1 statements revealed nothing that changes this, and I claim no recusal.
